name: Cyprus
summary: Drug use and possession are criminal offences under the 1977 Narcotic Drugs Law, with penalties by class (A/B/C); first-time offenders under 25 face at most 1 year and can be diverted to treatment.
callingForHelp: No specific Good Samaritan law found. Possession is criminal and police may become involved; health staff are bound by medical confidentiality.

lsd.note: Class A: possession up to 12 years' prison (first-time under-25s max 1 year); use is also an offence. Diversion to treatment is possible.

mushrooms.note: Psilocin is Class A, so psilocybin mushrooms are treated as a Class A drug: possession up to 12 years' prison.

dmt.note: DMT is Class A: possession up to 12 years' prison (first-time under-25s max 1 year).

mescaline.note: Mescaline is Class A: possession up to 12 years' prison (first-time under-25s max 1 year).

dox.note: DOM is listed in Class A; DOB/DOC are UN Schedule I and presumed controlled. Possession is a serious crime.

nbomes.note: NBOMes are UN Schedule I and presumed controlled; possession is a crime.

2c-x.note: 2C-B is UN Schedule II and presumed controlled; possession is a crime.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2/2C-T-7 are not UN-scheduled; could not confirm whether Cyprus lists them.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT are not UN-scheduled; could not confirm whether Cyprus lists them.

cannabis.note: Class B: possession up to 8 years' prison (first-time under-25s max 1 year); diversion to treatment possible. Medical cannabis is available.

ketamine.note: Prescription anaesthetic; could not confirm its class under Cypriot law. If controlled, non-prescribed possession is a crime.

mxe.note: UN Schedule II since 2016 and presumed controlled; possession is a crime.

dxm.note: Expressly excluded from the narcotics schedule; it is a cough medicine, but its prescription status was not confirmed.

nitrous.note: Not UN-scheduled; no national rule found in sources checked.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are Class B: possession up to 8 years' prison. Methylphenidate (Class B) is prescription-only.

mdma.note: Class A: possession up to 12 years' prison (first-time under-25s max 1 year); use is also an offence. Diversion to treatment is possible.

cocaine.note: Class A: possession up to 12 years' prison (first-time under-25s max 1 year); use is also an offence. Diversion to treatment is possible.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal; selling alcohol to under-17s is prohibited.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is UN Schedule II and presumed controlled; possession is a crime. GBL/1,4-BD status not confirmed.

opioids.note: Heroin, morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl are Class A: possession without prescription up to 12 years' prison. Prescription opioids medical-only.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only; Class C, so possession without a prescription can carry up to 4 years' prison.

maois.note: MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only. Status of harmala alkaloids/ayahuasca not confirmed (DMT is Class A).
